feasible.reason: The repo evidence checks out line-for-line: `pin_row` (secure/src/ui/px/status_map.rs:276-293) writes `b'0' + pin[i] % 10` into an Entry record that `rows::build_entry` (pqsigner-ui-px/src/rows.rs:76-90) emits as `Item::Text` through the address-indexed `Tier::glyph` (font.rs:72-80); `render_pin_screen` and `render_letter_screen` call `screens::show` (= `show_with(s, &[])`, screens.rs:127), so `play_screen` runs with `force=false` and `present_frame_ex` (lcd.rs:304-322) digests and skips strips derived from the secret pixel; the legacy branches route through `draw_line` → `public_glyph_cols` (secret_text.rs:88-93, direct index). `Item::Secret` has exactly one producer (`push_secret_word`), `blit_secret_run` scans only a-z (font.rs:234-235), F-20 draws all eight start digits once at session entry (pin_entry.rs:79-85), and the Trezor citation is real (pin.rs:89/170/326). So the MCU-side address channel and the strip-skip/digest residue are genuinely open, the CT primitives and forced-frame path exist, and the proposal is realisable in firmware without any hardware change, inside the no-heap/flash constraints (a per-pixel scan of ~36 candidates over one ring cell is negligible; a forced full-frame stream is ~28 ms, already the measured write time). It is not refuted. But the threat statement over-reaches, item (4) adds nothing, the px mechanics as written would paint in the wrong place, and the "host test" cannot observe the call sites it wants to pin — see corrections.
feasible.corrections:
1. Narrow the threat: the proposal does NOT defend the "EM/power probe on the NV3007 SPI stream" half. The dialed digit's RGB565 pixels travel in plaintext over MOSI on every frame regardless of how the glyph was fetched — this is exactly the F-24 stage-E residual the project already accepts (tools/sca/README.md F-24 table, font.rs:265-267 "only the pixel VALUES do"). What the change closes is (a) the MCU-side mem_address channel (stage D) and (b) the strip-skip timing + the 64-bit digest left in `static mut SHOWN`. On the SPI wire the only gain is uniform all-strips streaming. Write the threat as "MCU-side address/timing channel during PIN entry and seed restore", not SPI-stream recovery, or the claim invites a trivial bypass argument.
2. Drop or demote item (4) (Trezor-style re-randomise after each accepted digit): it yields no information-theoretic gain here. F-20 already draws an INDEPENDENT random start for each of the eight positions (pin_entry.rs:79-85); re-drawing position i+1 after accepting position i only differs from drawing it at session start for an attacker who can read SRAM between the two moments, and such an attacker reads `pin[]` directly. Trezor needs the re-draw because caesar keeps a single page counter for the active digit, not an 8-array. Mark it UX-neutral cosmetic parity, not a security item.
3. The px mechanics as written are wrong: `show_with`'s `secret` slice is `(word-grid cell k, 8-byte zero-padded word)` painted by `push_secret_word` at `grid_cell(k)` with `TierId::regular(22)` on a 14 px pitch (rows.rs:197-208; `blit_secret_run` hard-codes `SECRET_CELLS = 8`, `SECRET_ADV`). The entry row places glyphs at ring centres (`x0 + i*RING_PITCH`, `CIRCLE_CY - ACTIVE_LIFT`, `TierId::semibold(22)`, rows.rs:60-90). Passing the digit through `show_with(&row, &secret)` would paint it in the word grid, not in the active ring. The real change is: a single-cell secret blit (`blit_secret_cell(tier, byte, cx, cy)` with a digit+letter candidate set, or two runs) and `build_entry` emitting `Item::Secret` for state `'A'` cells from bytes supplied out-of-record, plus a `force` flag (or non-empty secret) on the present path. Verify the semibold-22 tier bakes 0-9 and a-z (it must, since entry draws them today). Cost is therefore S/M rather than S — still small, but it is a new blit primitive + builder change, not "two call sites and one builder".
4. Item (3) cannot be the host test described: `pin_entry.rs` and `seed_wizard.rs` live under `mod ui`, which is `#[cfg(not(test))]` (secure/src/main.rs:282-283), so no host test can observe whether they call `show` or `show_with`. What CAN be host-tested is that `pin_row`/`letter_row` records contain only placeholder glyphs (no 0-9/a-z in the glyph array). Enforce the "never through show()" half structurally: have the secret-bearing builders return a `SecretScreen` newtype that only `show_with`-style presenters accept (or a semgrep rule), so the type system, not a test, closes the regression.
5. Legacy part (1) is fine as stated: `secret_glyph_cols` scans all 96 ASCII glyphs so digits are already covered, and `flush_with_secret_rows` (lcd.rs:180) takes `(row, bytes)`; render the whole PIN/letter row through it so the secret cell's column is not distinguished either.
6. Priority P0 → P1. #784 itself is rated medium; the attacker needs an EM probe on the MCU during the owner's PIN entry, and the same digit is simultaneously broadcast in plaintext over SPI (accepted residual). Worth doing because it is cheap and the invariant is already written down, but it is parity hygiene, not a ship-blocker. Must be validated with `make e2e-px` (ui-px path compiled IN) and re-run of the F-24 glyph-leak TVLA harness with the widened candidate set to confirm the `black_box` barriers still hold (secret_text.rs:44-50 regression mode).

vendor-claim.corrections: 1) Novelty should be split per sub-item, not a single 'parity'. Sub-item (4) per-digit re-randomisation is exact parity with Trezor caesar (pin.rs:322-326); note Trezor delizia instead Fisher-Yates-shuffles the whole keypad (layout_delizia/component/keyboard/pin.rs:298-300, random::shuffle) and Trezor One randomly permutes the 3x3 matrix (legacy/firmware/pinmatrix.c:57-63) — both are shoulder-surf/button-count defences, not display-SCA defences. Sub-items (1)-(3) (constant-time glyph lookup + forced full-strip SPI streaming + no digest residue + host regression test) have NO vendor precedent found: Trezor's 9b1c06205c is CT in seed PROCESSING (mnemonic_to_bits / mnemonic_find_word), not in rendering; grep of core/embed + legacy for side-channel/constant-time hits only random_delays, consteq, PIN digest compare (legacy/firmware/config.c:793) — nothing in the UI/display layers; Coldcard v2.1.2 only stops echoing PIN digits and adds right-side masking noise on seed rows (blog.coinkite.com/noise-troll). So (1)-(3) are 'beyond' on the CPU/SPI-side channel. 2) However, Ledger's 2023 PIN screen attacks a DIFFERENT, panel-side channel (F-24 stage E sub-channels 2/3: lit-pixel-count power/EM of the panel itself) by making the per-row illuminated pixel count digit-independent; this proposal leaves that channel open — a forced CT frame still paints a different glyph per digit, so panel draw stays digit-dependent (tools/sca/README.md:1265-1300 lists stage E as hardware-territory/accepted; the archived 'Phase 2 constant-pixel-count encoding' is deferred, docs/archive/work-todo-retired-2026-07-19.md:2488). Recommend adding a sub-item (5): a Ledger-style constant-pixel-load PIN/letter widget (fixed ring of all ten digits / all letters always drawn, only a marker moves — equivalently the Trezor One always-full matrix), which would make the card genuinely 'beyond' on both channels; without it, state novelty as 'beyond (CPU/SPI side), below Ledger 2023 (panel pixel-load side)'. 3) Precedent wording fixes: 'Ledger 1.6/2023' should read 'Ledger LSB-006 (Aug 2019, CVE-2019-14354, Nano S/X SSD1306; first mitigation = randomised display parameters/colour inversion in Q4-2019 firmware) and the Jan 2023 Nano X / S Plus constant-pixel-count PIN UI' — the bulletin and blog name no '1.6' firmware version. Trezor legacy also shipped 'OLED display security improvements' in 1.8.2 (legacy/firmware/CHANGELOG.md:331-334, Aug 2019) as its response to the same Donjon OLED class — worth citing as precedent that both major vendors treated the display as a power side-channel surface. 4) Minor: the Trezor line cite should be pin.rs:322-326 (set_page_counter) and :168-170 (initial), and the Trezor CT bip39 commit is dated 2025-11-12 (cherry-pick of 4e6f0dee81), so it is very recent precedent, not long-standing.
